about.title: Bell Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products turn up everywhere in Bell — a car part that fails on the I-710, a tool used on the job near the industrial stretches off Gage Avenue, a household appliance that malfunctions at home. When a product hurts someone, California law often lets the injured person pursue a claim under strict liability, meaning the focus is on whether the product was defective, not on proving the manufacturer was careless. That's a meaningful difference for families in Bell who are already dealing with medical bills and lost income. Manufacturers, distributors, and even retailers can share responsibility depending on how the product moved through the supply chain. If you were hurt by something that didn't work the way it should have, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney, free of charge, who can look at what happened and explain your options. There's no obligation, and no fee unless the attorney recovers something for you.

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters for Your Claim

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: Under California law, you generally don't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent — just that the product was defective and caused your injury. This can make it easier to hold a company accountable.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all be named in a product liability claim depending on their role in getting the defective item to you. An attorney can help identify every party who may be liable.

items.title: Preserving the Product Protects Your Case
items.desc: Keeping the item that caused your injury — rather than discarding or repairing it — helps preserve evidence a lawyer can later evaluate for design, manufacturing, or warning defects.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability rule generally lets you focus on showing the product itself was defective and that the defect caused your injury, rather than proving negligence. An independent attorney can walk you through how this applies to your specific situation.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the condition it was in right after the incident, without repairing or discarding it. This preserves it as evidence that an attorney or expert may need to examine later.

items.question: I was hurt by a defective part on the I-710 in Bell — does that count as product liability?
items.answer: It might. If a vehicle part, tire, or safety component failed and contributed to your crash, that could point to a defect claim in addition to any other issues involved. An attorney can review the details and let you know how it fits together.

items.question: Is there a cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you.
